title: Into the pit (Genesis 37:12–36)
hookLine: the brothers throw Joseph in a pit and sell him; Reuben comes back too late

lines: THEY SEE HIM FROM FAR OFF.
cards: The brothers are far from home, pasturing the flocks, when Jacob sends Joseph to check on them. From a long way off, they see him coming. Maybe it's the coat they recognize first.
They say to each other: "Behold, this dreamer cometh." Let's kill him, throw him in a pit, and say a wild animal ate him. Then we'll see what becomes of his dreams.
Out in the fields, with no father watching, a family grudge turns into a plan.

teach.h: REUBEN: JUST THROW HIM IN THE PIT.
teach.b: Reuben, the oldest, speaks up. Don't kill him; just throw him into this pit. The Torah tells us his secret plan: come back later, pull Joseph out, and bring him home to their father.
So they strip off the coat and throw Joseph in, and the text adds a detail: "the pit was empty, there was no water in it."

teach.h: THEY SIT DOWN TO EAT BREAD.
teach.b: Then, while Joseph is down there, they sit down to eat bread. A caravan passes, traders going down to Egypt. Judah has an idea: what do we gain by killing him?

teach.h: SOLD FOR TWENTY PIECES OF SILVER.
teach.b: And Joseph is sold for twenty pieces of silver. The text gets a little tangled here about who pulled him out and who sold him, and readers still puzzle over it. And Reuben?

teach.h: REUBEN COMES BACK TO AN EMPTY PIT.
teach.b: He comes back to the pit, and it's empty.
He tears his clothes: "The child is not; and as for me, whither shall I go?" The midrash has a sharp line about this.

Had Reuben known that the Torah would write down that he tried to save Joseph, it says, he would have picked him up on his shoulders and carried him home to his father right then. The good intention was real.

The delay cost everything. Then the brothers dip the coat in goat's blood and bring it to Jacob, and he says, "an evil beast hath devoured him." He tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth, and refuses to be comforted.

how: Some Jewish teachers use Reuben's delay to talk about acting on a good impulse right away, echoing the saying in Pirkei Avot, if not now, when?

games.q: you're Reuben. your brothers want to kill Joseph. you're the oldest, but you're outnumbered. what do you do?
o: fight all of them to stop it.

games.why: he talks them down to the pit and plans a rescue. but he isn't there when it matters, and when he returns, the pit is empty.

practice: Think of one good thing you've been meaning to come back to: an apology, a call to someone who's alone, a word in someone's defense. Picture the first minute of actually doing it, then notice what's been stopping you.

wordCard.voice: Bor, Hebrew for a pit or cistern, the empty one where Joseph was thrown. Joseph is thrown into an empty pit and sold, while the brother who meant to save him is somewhere else.
